articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dumps AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like sharing vacation photos. Because nothing says 'cybersecurity expertise' like accidentally publishing the keys to the kingdom for script kiddies to find.

articles.title: Zscaler Announces Strong Third-Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results
articles.summary: KnowledgeDeliver LMS got schooled by hackers exploiting a zero-day to drop Godzilla web shells. The irony of a 'knowledge delivery' system delivering backdoors instead is *chef's kiss* perfect.

articles.title: Sunrise Movement Backs Saikat Chakrabarti, Progressive Firebrand Behind the Green New Deal
articles.summary: Megalodon malware devoured 5,500 GitHub repos in six hours, proving that supply chain attacks are the new ransomware. Your favorite open source project might be serving credentials as a side dish.

articles.title: 3 SOC Steps that Shut Down Incident Risks Early
articles.summary: CrowdStrike and Google teamed up to nuke GlassWorm's entire C2 infrastructure targeting developers. Finally, some good news in the eternal hellscape of supply chain compromises.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: License plate readers have evolved from catching actual criminals to enforcing school enrollment and noise complaints. Because apparently Big Brother needed a hobby that involves tracking every grocery store run.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a rare victory for end-to-end encryption in their latest newsletter. In these dark times, we'll take any W we can get for keeping our digital conversations away from three-letter agencies.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Evolution: How We Went From Perimeter Defense to AI-Native Security
articles.summary: AI is now helping script kiddies speedrun exploit development faster than security scanners can keep up. The machines aren't taking over—they're just making the humans better at breaking stuff.

articles.title: Latin American Cybercriminals Hoover Up Government Data
articles.summary: Silent Ransom Group literally shows up at law firms pretending to be tech support to steal data. Old school social engineering meets modern extortion—sometimes the classics never go out of style.

articles.title: reconprobe added to PyPI
articles.summary: TrapDoor malware targets crypto developers with supply chain attacks that manipulate AI coding assistants. Because apparently poisoning the well wasn't enough—now they're corrupting the AI that writes the code that drinks from the well.

articles.title: 5 Steps to Managing Shadow AI Tools Without Slowing Down Employees
articles.summary: Malicious npm package specifically designed to pillage Claude AI's user directory and exfiltrate files via GitHub. Even our AI overlords can't escape having their digital pockets picked by crafty malware.
